1. Introduction

The African Union Development Agency – New Partnership for Africa Development (AUDA-NEPAD) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the “Resilient Irrigation for a Sustainable Economy Project”, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. “Consultancy Services to Develop and Deploy the Africa RISE Gateway”

 

  1. Description of Services

The consulting services (“the Services”) include: Task 1: Africa RISE User Requirements Assessment: Map and profile all user groups and partners including relevant African Union agencies and departments (AUDANEPAD, AU-SAFGRAD, SEBE), government ministries, transboundary water management agencies, regulators, MPA focal points, implementing partners, research institutes and universities and technical experts, farmers, aggregators, private sector, equipment suppliers and financial institutions and farmer unions and cooperative societies etc; Task 2: Design, Develop and Commission the Africa RISE Gateway: Define system architecture, data structures, modules, dashboard requirements and proc

ISE User Requirements Assessment: Map and profile all user groups and partners including relevant African Union agencies and departments (AUDANEPAD, AU-SAFGRAD, SEBE), government ministries, transboundary water management agencies, regulators, MPA focal points, implementing partners, research institutes and universities and technical experts, farmers, aggregators, private sector, equipment suppliers and financial institutions and farmer unions and cooperative societies etc; Task 2: Design, Develop and Commission the Africa RISE Gateway: Define system architecture, data structures, modules, dashboard requirements and process workflows, including a unified data interoperability Layer that meets vPIC standards and aligns with the Africa RISE Regional Geospatial Analytics Platform and national irrigation monitoring systems.  The architecture shall specify: (a) the endpoints and payload schemas through which national data collection tools, the Regional Geospatial Platform,  and other authorized external data sources submit and validate benchmarking data; (b) the data lineage and version control mechanisms ensuring that published benchmarks are traceable to their submission source; and (c) the traffic-light alert logic that translates performanc

sociated training materials for all user groups, comprising: (i) a Technical Track for AUDA-NEPAD IT personnel, national technical focal points and system administrators, covering system administration, data management, integration and cybersecurity; (ii) an Operational Track for programme managers, extension officers and policy stakeholders, focusing on effective use of the platform and its functional modules; and (iii) an End-User Track providing simplified guidance and orientation materials. STATEMENT OF WORK C. 1. OVERVIEW/BACKGROUND. The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory

The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats. NLS requires additional DA2 units, consistent with the existing inventory of NLS DA2 devices. NLS requires quantities suffi

SCOPE OF WORK The vendor will develop and implement a creative, physical messaging campaign to publicize safe, official repatriation mechanisms in target communities across Honduras. Activities will include the design, procurement, and deployment of everyday, high-turnover physical media—such as reusable bags, food packaging, or other take-home items—to deliver messaging about repatriation mechanisms to the family members of Honduran nationals currently residing illegally in the United States. To realize this initiative, the selected organization will be responsible for building strategic relationships with private sector micro-logistics networks, small business owners, commercial brands, or community merchant associations across five Honduran cities to successfully disseminate and deploy the branded materials directly into target zones. f_Work.docx ===== STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) RFID Cabinet The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), requires the acquisition of a Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) storage cabinet integrated with Unique Device Identifier (UDI)-compliant tissue and implant tracking software to support patient safety, regulatory compliance, and efficient inventory management. Tracking tissues, biologics, and implantable medical devices is a federal regulatory requirement under FDA 21 CFR Part 830 (UDI) and is critical to patient safety. VA healthcare facilities face ongoing resource challenges including staff shortages and budget constraints, making it essential to minimize staff time consumed by manual data entry and to maintain precise control over high-value inventory. This acquisition will provide an automated, real-time RFID-based inventory management solution for use in the operating room (OR), Catheterization (Cath) lab, ambulatory surgery center, or any facility location that stores high-value implantable inventory. If any conflict exists between instructions/submissions stated in CSO HT003826SC005 and this AOI #01, this AOI #01 shall prevail. 2 1.0 Executive Summary & Strategic Context 1.1 Military Health System (MHS) Mission The MHS is one of the largest and most complex healthcare enterprises in the world. It is a globally integrated system serving over 9.6 million beneficiaries, including active-duty service members, retirees, and their families. The MHS is unique in that it functions as both a direct healthcare provider and a multi-billion-dollar health insurance payer through the TRICARE program. Its ultimate success

e medical capabilities, austere mission environments, field hospitals and Forward Operating Bases. DoW’s close relationship with the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is paramount. The success of an integrated Federal Electronic Health Record (EHR) is a top national priority. Equally critical is the ability to support the continuum of care across operational and enterprise healthcare environments, ensuring that health information generated during military operations can be captured, exchanged, and made available to support continued care within the enterprise health record. Together, these operational, enterprise, and interagency requirements create a highly complex healthcare ecosystem that includes deployed medical environments, fixed medical treatment facilities, the Federal Health Care Center and other DoW/VA sharing sites. Supporting the ecosystem requires coordinated end user service models and highly configurable enterprise approaches capable of operating across diverse mission environments while enabling interoperability, continuity of care, and interagency collaboration. 1.2 EUS Overview & Transition Strategy To maximize the value of the Department’s health technology investments, PAE MDS is transitioning from legacy, labor-intensive support contracts to a unifie

le DDIL Operations: Ensure training, adoption, and communication resources are available offline and locally to support operational units in Denied, Disrupted, Intermittent, and Limited (DDIL) environments. Maintain a deployable surge capacity to provide short-notice, onsite tactical training, workflow support, and physical setup/teardown of training hardware during military exercises. • Parallel Innovation Framework: Establish a low-risk framework to test, scale, and deploy automated workflows and novel technologies in a live environment without "hard cutovers" that risk clinical downtime. 2.2 Governance, XLAs, Enforcement, & Modern Deliverables Problem Statement: Legacy user-facing services suffer from fragmented governance, static administrative reporting, and unregulated product intake. As used in this provision- "Eligible contractor" means a business entity operated on a for-profit or nonprofit basis that- (1) Employs severely disabled individuals at a rate that averages not less than 33 percent of its total workforce over the 12-month period prior to issuance of the solicitation; (2) Pays not less than the minimum wage prescribed pursuant to 29 U.S.C. 206 to the employees who are severely disabled individuals; and (3) Provides, for its employees, health insurance and a retirement plan comparable to those provided for employees by business entities of similar size in its industrial sector or geographic region. "Severely disabled individual" means an individual with a disability (as defined in 42 U.S.C. 12102) who has a severe physical or mental impairment that seriously limits one or more functional capacities.
